title: 2006 AMC 12B Problem 15
statement: Circles with centers \(O\) and \(P\) have radii \(2\) and \(4,\) respectively, and are externally tangent. Points \(A\) and \(B\) are on the circle centered at \(O,\) and points \(C\) and \(D\) are on the circle centered at \(P,\) such that \(AD\) and \(BC\) are common external tangents to the circles. What is the area of hexagon \(AOBCPD?\)

solutions.text:
The circles are externally tangent, so \(OP = 2 + 4 = 6.\) In quadrilateral \(AOPD,\) both \(OA = 2\) and \(PD = 4\) are perpendicular to the tangent line \(AD,\) making it a right trapezoid.

Drawing the line through \(O\) parallel to \(AD\) creates a right triangle with hypotenuse \(OP = 6\) and one leg \(PD - OA = 2,\) so \(AD = \sqrt{6^2 - 2^2} = \sqrt{32} = 4\sqrt2.\)

The trapezoid \(AOPD\) has area \[\frac{1}{2}(2 + 4)(4\sqrt2) = 12\sqrt2.\]

By symmetry the hexagon \(AOBCPD\) is made of two such trapezoids, so its area is \(2 \cdot 12\sqrt2 = 24\sqrt2.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: The centers are \(OP = 2 + 4 = 6\) apart, and the radii to the tangent points are perpendicular to the tangent
\(AOPD\) is a right trapezoid; find its slant side with the Pythagorean theorem, then double the area
